- If sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.75) in recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slightly, especially after spikes.
- If sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model often underestimates; increase forecast modestly, especially in early horizon.
- Model frequently overshoots after recent price spikes; apply a 1–2 day lag correction or dampen peak forecasts.
- When sentiment shifts from positive to negative, model often fails to adjust downward; apply downward bias correction in next 3–5 days.
- Mean reversion is evident in 30-day forecasts: if forecast is > 10% above recent 18-day average, reduce by 5–10% unless sentiment supports continuation.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome is consistently below forecast, model may be overfitting recent volatility; use sentiment-weighted smoothing to reduce noise.
